label: Low budget, how to make it cinematic?
q: I'm a student director with almost no budget and basic gear. How do I use blocking and camera work to make my short feel cinematic?

label: How to design a long take that doesn't fall apart?
q: I want a single unbroken long take, but camera moves and actor blocking keep falling apart. Is there a method to design long takes?

label: Why does my second act drag?
q: Act one and three of my script are fine, but act two is bloated and the rhythm collapses. How do I tighten the second act?

label: How to direct non-actors to real emotion?
q: I cast some non-professionals as leads, but they freeze in front of the camera and read lines like a textbook. How do I get genuine performances from non-actors?

label: Grade looks cheap — how to build a consistent look?
q: My footage is decent, but the grade looks cheap and shots don't match across scenes. How do I build one unified visual tone for the whole film?

label: Dialogue scenes feel dead — how to liven them?
q: This scene is basically two people sitting and talking, and it plays flat, like reading a script. How do I use lens, framing and sound to make dialogue scenes alive?

label: How to get Wong Kar-wai's texture?
q: I love Wong Kar-wai's ambiguous light and detached mood. From art direction and lighting to camera movement, what concrete techniques get me close to that texture?

label: Can a phone shoot something with real texture?
q: I have no pro gear, just a phone. Can a phone actually produce textured, cinematic shorts? What should I watch for?
